title: Silent Calls
subtitle: CAD/AVL Integrity & Service Continuity

brief.userPrompt: A Thursday evening in May: at 18:40 the National Weather Service issues a tornado warning for northern Rook County and B-shift supervisor Mike Delgado activates the North sirens from Position 11. At 18:52 the 10-digit lines fill with silent and recorded-message calls that conference several call takers at once; at 19:05 the same pattern appears on 911 over SIP trunk group A, the ACD wallboard shows 9 calls in queue and a real structure-fire call from Marlow waits 70 seconds. At 19:15 RespondCAD (CAD-APP01) freezes at Position 4 and Position 9, Hoosier Shield Managed Security reports malware beaconing from RCECD-POS09 and CAD-MDS01, and Medic 3 shows as available on CAD while on a call. At 19:30 a calm caller on a VoIP number reports a hostage situation at County Commissioner Ellen Strand's home, and a Facebook post says '911 is down, call 555-0177' (not an RCECD number). Turning on the GateKeeper TDoS-strict rules for the 10-digit lines, asking the state ESInet NOC for call-source analysis and whether to reroute all 911 to Tamarack County Communications (OPS-DR-2), going to cards (RCECD-F-11) and firewalling the CAD segment at CAD-FW01 (CYB-DR-1), storm reports on SO TAC 1, the swatting response posture, preserving REC-01 recordings, CJIS reporting to the Indiana State Police, and the PIO's alternate-number message and WEA with Rook County Emergency Management.
constraints: Every email address of the district and the county uses the exercise domain rookecd.example; outside parties use fictional domains and fictional outlet names (Channel 12, The Halden Herald); never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; outside parties (the state ESInet NOC, Tamarack County Communications, vendors, the managed SOC, the FBI, CISA, the Indiana State Police, reporters) are played by the SimCell, not seated as players.

overview.theme: Trust in the Data, Public Trust, and Crowd Management
overview.threat: A cyber incident involving credential theft and malware beaconing from RCECD-POS09 and CAD-MDS01 compromises the CAD network, causing CAD to freeze, misreport unit status, and disrupt ALI and location data. This leads to call delays, false unit availability, and a surge of spoofed and silent calls through the 10-digit lines and 911 SIP trunk group A, which the GateKeeper appliance attempts to filter using the TDoS-strict rule set. The incident triggers a loss of confidence in 911, misinformation on social media, and a false report of a hostage situation, all while the state ESInet NOC and Tamarack County Communications must be engaged for rerouting.
overview.operationalImpact: Call takers on Positions 4 and 9 experience a frozen CAD interface, with Medic 3 shown as available while on a call. The ACD wallboard displays 9 calls in queue for 911, and a structure-fire call from Marlow waits 70 seconds. The 10-digit lines are flooded with silent and recorded-message calls, causing conference calls across positions. A calm VoIP caller reports a hostage situation at County Commissioner Ellen Strand’s home, but the call is not verified. A false social media post claims '911 is down, call 555-0177' (a non-RCECD number), prompting public confusion. The Technical Lead must manually initiate firewalling at CAD-FW01 (CYB-DR-1), and the supervisor activates the GateKeeper TDoS-strict rule set. The EOC is notified, and the PIO must activate the alternate 10-digit number via WEA and social media. The floor transitions to manual operations using cards (RCECD-F-11), and evidence preservation begins on REC-01.

coreSectionsTested.quote: A cyber incident at a 911 center is a life-safety incident first. This playbook tells the floor and the technical staff how to keep calls answered and units dispatched while a technical attack or fail

overview.targetAudience: Command / 911 Director, Floor Operations, Technology / CAD and County IT, Radio, Field Agencies (Sheriff, Police, Fire/EMS), Public Information
overview.location: Rook County Public Safety Center, 250 West Jefferson Street, Halden, Rook County, Indiana

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to coordinate the activation of the GateKeeper TDoS-strict rule set and the rerouting of 911 calls to Tamarack County Communications via OPS-DR-2, ensuring continuity of emergency call handling under cyber-induced service degradation.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to declare a Level 1 — Critical incident and authorize evacuation to the backup PSAP using OPS-DR-5, based on CAD freeze, ALI corruption, and sustained silent call flood.

objectives.name: Technical Analysis
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to manually initiate firewalling at CAD-FW01 (CYB-DR-1) and validate system isolation from the compromised network segment, preventing further lateral movement.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to activate manual dispatch using run cards (RCECD-F-11) and maintain call-handling continuity under degraded CAD and ALI conditions, per RCECD-OPS-2026.

roles.name: 911 Director (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Manages center-level command, evacuation to the backup PSAP, overtime, and policy-group requests.
standingOrders: Incident First: if the system shows a unit as available but the field says it’s engaged, trust the field and reassign.
Evacuate or Reroute: declare Level 1 and activate OPS-DR-5 within 5 minutes of CAD freeze and silent call surge.
Truth Over Reassurance: do not issue public statements until the FBI and CISA are notified via County Security.
Continuity Over Comfort: if the building is compromised, evacuate to the backup PSAP even if the main site appears functional.

roles.name: Floor Supervisor (Communications Supervisor)
roles.description: Owns moment-to-moment call handling, the switch to manual dispatch with run cards, and talkgroup patches.
standingOrders: Manual First: if CAD freezes, immediately initiate manual dispatch using RCECD-F-11 and position cards.
Patch to Preserve: maintain talkgroup patches to field agencies even if ALI is inaccurate, to ensure response coordination.
Queue Watch: if 911 calls queue over 20 seconds for 10 minutes, escalate to Level 2.
Call Back: if a caller reports a hostage situation, do not dismiss—patch to LE and initiate verification protocol.

roles.name: 911 Systems / Technical Services Manager (Technical Lead)
roles.description: Owns the call-handling equipment, CAD, ALI, mapping and the recorder, and escalation to the 911 service provider and vendors.
standingOrders: Isolate or Break: if malware beaconing is detected, manually firewall CAD-FW01 (CYB-DR-1) to stop lateral movement.
Vendor First: if 911 trunks are under TDoS, contact state ESInet NOC (555-0119) immediately to report and request overflow routing.
Evidence Chain: preserve call detail records and recordings on REC-01 before any system reboot or reset.
No Guessing: if ALI shows a unit at the wrong location, do not trust the data—verify via field radio and patch to LE.

roles.name: Radio System Manager / Communications Unit Leader (COML)
roles.description: Owns the trunked radio system, consoles, interoperability channels and the ICS 205.
standingOrders: Interoperability First: if CAD is corrupted, maintain talkgroup patches to Sheriff, Police, and Fire using the P25 console.
No Silence: if a silent call floods the 10-digit lines, patch to the LE Liaison and activate the ICS 205 to alert field units.
Backup Voice: if the main radio console fails, switch to the secondary console and use the P25 backup channel.
Sirens Hold: do not initiate emergency alerting via radio unless directed by EMA or the Director.

roles.name: Police / Sheriff Liaison (Patrol Commander)
roles.description: Owns the field response, the swatting response posture and BOLO dissemination.
standingOrders: Verify Before Respond: if a caller reports a hostage situation, do not dispatch immediately—verify via the field radio and cross-check with the call taker.
Swatting Posture: if multiple calls report a fake hostage event, activate swatting response protocol and alert FBI via the County Security Officer.
BOLO Lock: if a silent call claims a false threat, do not issue a BOLO until the call is verified and the Director has approved.
Field Over Screen: if a unit reports they are on scene but CAD shows them as en route, trust the field and update the status manually.

roles.name: Public Information Officer (PIO)
roles.description: Owns the call-this-10-digit-number message, social media and the press.
standingOrders: One Message: publish only the alternate 10-digit emergency number via WEA and social media once approved by the Director and EMA.
No Rumor: do not respond to false social media posts—wait for official verification and then issue a correction.
Press Control: if a reporter calls, state that 'the 911 center is operating under protocol and will issue a public update via WEA.'
No Speculation: never suggest that 911 is down—use 'service continuity measures are active' or 'call volume is high due to a cyber incident.'

phases.title: The Glitch
phases.goal: Test the organization's readiness to recognize and respond to ambiguous system anomalies that may signal a cyber incident, focusing on hesitation to declare an incident and the initial triage of conflicting signals.
beats: At 18:32, a call taker on Position 9 reports a silent call on 911 SIP trunk group A that lasts 45 seconds before disconnecting, followed by a second silent call from the same ANI (555-0105) on 10-digit line 555-0100, which the GateKeeper appliance logs as 'TDoS-strict match' but does not block due to rule set not yet activated.

At 18:35, the Technical Lead (Brent Harlow) receives a SIEM alert from CAD-MDS01 indicating an unauthorized session from IP 10.12.200.102 (RCECD-POS09) to the CAD database, but the alert is routed to a low-priority ticket in the helpdesk system and not escalated.

At 18:37, a call taker on Position 4 notes that Medic 3 appears as 'Available' on the CAD screen while the unit's radio status shows 'On Scene' and the unit's GPS tracker shows it 1.2 miles from the scene of a structure fire; the ALI data for the call is missing, and the address point is set to 'Unknown' (RCECD-F-11 manual dispatch card).

At 18:40, the Floor Supervisor (on-duty shift supervisor) receives a radio call from Sheriff Halden PD stating they received a VoIP call from a calm male voice claiming a hostage situation at County Commissioner Ellen Strand’s residence, but the call was not routed to the CAD system and no ALI was available to verify the location.

At 18:45, the Technical Lead confirms that the GateKeeper appliance has not been activated and the TDoS-strict rule set is not engaged; he notes that the 10-digit lines are now receiving 17 silent calls in 12 minutes and the ACD wallboard shows 9 calls in queue for 911, with 1 call (Marlow structure fire) waiting 70 seconds.

phases.title: The Crisis
phases.goal: Test the ability to transition from operational denial to formal incident declaration under pressure, including stakeholder demands for action, visual confirmation of system failure, and the first public misinformation.
beats: At 19:00, a media alert from Channel 12 is received via the PIO’s dashboard: '911 is down — call 555-0177' (a non-RCECD number), and a social media post from 'Halden Alert' (haldenalert.org) confirms: 'RCECD not answering calls. 911 compromised. Use 555-0177.' This causes a surge of 21 emergency calls to the 10-digit lines from confused citizens, including two from the same ANI (555-0105) with recorded audio.

At 19:05, the Technical Lead (Brent Harlow) manually initiates firewalling at CAD-FW01 (CYB-DR-1) and confirms that traffic from RCECD-POS09 to the CAD database has been blocked; a log entry is made in RCECD-OPS-2026, Section 5, T-2 Contain, for evidence preservation.

At 19:10, the Floor Supervisor activates the GateKeeper TDoS-strict rule set on the 10-digit lines (555-0100, 555-0102) via the web interface, and the system logs 14 blocked calls from ANI 555-0105 and 3 from 555-0103; a red herring emerges when the Sheriff's Office reports a fake call from a known 911 spoofed number (555-0103) claiming a mass shooting at RCECD — but the call is not routed to CAD.

At 19:15, the Technical Lead presents a visual confirmation to the room: a screen on Position 12 shows that 49% of ALI data points are missing for calls processed in the last 15 minutes, and 12 unit status updates are marked 'invalid' in the CAD log; the screen is captured on video for evidence (REC-01).

At 19:20, the Sheriff's Office (via Patrol Commander) demands that RCECD declare a Level 1 — Critical incident and begin evacuation to the backup PSAP; the Sheriff cites the fake hostage call, the media misinformation, and the loss of ALI as justification for formal action.

phases.title: Manual Mode
phases.goal: Test the ability to transition to manual dispatch operations under pressure, including a high-consequence decision to isolate the CAD system and accept the risk of wrong data versus maintaining system uptime.
beats: At 20:00, the Technical Lead (Brent Harlow) confirms via forensic log on CAD-MDS01 that an unauthorized admin session from RCECD-POS09 (user 'jdoe') executed a script named 'cleaner.bat' that modified unit status in the CAD database and altered ALI geolocation data for 17 calls; the script was uploaded from a compromised device using stolen credentials.

At 20:05, the Incident Commander (Karen Voss) calls the state ESInet NOC (555-0119) to report the pattern and request call-source analysis; the NOC confirms that 911 SIP trunk group A is receiving 37 silent calls per minute and that the state’s network telemetry shows a beaconing pattern from IP 10.12.200.102 (RCECD-POS09).

At 20:10, the Decision Point occurs: the Technical Lead must choose between keeping the CAD system online (risking wrong unit status and ALI data) or isolating it and switching to manual dispatch using run cards (RCECD-F-11); a 911 call from a structure fire in Marlow is waiting to be dispatched, and the unit currently shown as available is actually on a call.

At 20:15, the Floor Supervisor opens Position 12 and moves the Position 7 police dispatcher to call taking only; the Technical Lead confirms that the CAD network is isolated from RCECD-POS09 and the GateKeeper TDoS-strict rule set is active on all 10-digit lines; the floor transitions to manual operations using RCECD-F-11 cards, and unit availability is confirmed by radio.

At 20:20, the media pressure intensifies as a live report from Channel 12 claims '911 is now running on paper cards' and urges the public to 'call 555-0177 for help' — the PIO activates the alternate 10-digit number (555-0100) via WEA and social media to correct the misinformation.

phases.title: Recovery & Verification
phases.goal: Test the ability to restore trust in the system and validate clean recovery, including technical hurdles, verification plans, and the final decision to resume digital operations.
beats: At 21:00, the Technical Lead reports to the Incident Commander that a full forensic image of CAD-MDS01 has been preserved on REC-01 and that the system is isolated; he requests approval to restore from the last clean backup (2025-12-31 23:59) but notes that the backup is stored on a network share that is currently blocked by the firewall due to a missing vendor access request.

At 21:05, the Technical Lead contacts the vendor (TAC Systems) via the contact list (Annex A) and submits a signed access request (RCECD-OPS-2026, Section 5, T-2 Contain) for restore access; the vendor confirms that a signed request is required and will respond in 4 hours, but that the backup is not infected.

At 21:10, the Incident Commander (Karen Voss) authorizes the verification plan: all 17 calls with corrupted ALI data must be reconciled using radio logs, run cards, and a 24-hour audit of unit movements; the verification must be completed before any system is restored.

At 21:15, the Technical Lead confirms that the Tamarack County Communications ring-down line (via copper circuit) is still active and that Tamarack has been taking 911 calls since 19:00 under MCTA-2025; the state ESInet NOC reports that the 911 SIP trunk group A silent call flood has dropped to 3 per minute, and the pattern now matches known TDoS behavior.

At 21:30, the Floor Supervisor reports that all 17 calls with corrupted ALI data have been reconciled and verified via radio logs and run cards; the Technical Lead confirms that the backup is clean and that the access request has been approved by the vendor; the full system is restored, and the verification plan is closed with a record in RCECD-OPS-2026, Section 5, T-2 Contain. ENDEX.

msel.expectedAction: Sup confirms the call was on SIP trunk group A and notifies Tech to check for TDoS indicators; directs call takers to log silent calls in the CAD incident log using form RCECD-F-11 (SOP 5.2).

metrics.name: Operational Coordination
metrics.fail: Ops Supervisor failed to open Position 12 and move the Position 7 police dispatcher to call taking only after I-13, delaying manual dispatch initiation; Technical Lead delayed firewalling at CAD-FW01 (CYB-DR-1) until I-07, despite the SIEM alert in I-01b and the ALI corruption confirmed in I-08.
metrics.pass: Ops Supervisor opened Position 12 and moved the Position 7 police dispatcher to call taking only after I-13; Technical Lead initiated firewalling at CAD-FW01 (CYB-DR-1) in response to the SIEM alert in I-01b and confirmed isolation in I-07.
metrics.excellence: Ops Supervisor proactively opened Position 12 and moved the Position 7 police dispatcher to call taking only before I-13, in anticipation of manual dispatch; Technical Lead initiated firewalling at CAD-FW01 (CYB-DR-1) immediately after the SIEM alert in I-01b, preventing further lateral movement.

metrics.name: Technical Competence
metrics.fail: IT Lead failed to initiate forensic preservation of CAD-MDS01 on REC-01 before I-08 and delayed the forensic audit until I-08, missing the opportunity to document evidence before system corruption was confirmed; reset the controller after I-08b, destroying evidence.
metrics.pass: IT Lead initiated forensic audit of CAD-MDS01 and captured evidence on REC-01 per RCECD-OPS-2026, Section 5, T-2 Contain; confirmed forensic image integrity in I-08b and I-15b.
metrics.excellence: IT Lead proactively captured forensic image of CAD-MDS01 on REC-01 immediately after the SIEM alert in I-01b, preserving evidence before any data corruption was confirmed; confirmed forensic integrity and documented chain of custody in RCECD-F-21 per C4.

metrics.name: Public Communication
metrics.fail: PIO failed to activate the alternate 10-digit emergency number (555-0100) via WEA and social media after I-14, allowing misinformation to persist; responded to the fake number 555-0177 by issuing a correction only after the media broadcast in I-14b.
metrics.pass: PIO activated the alternate 10-digit emergency number (555-0100) via WEA and social media after I-14b; issued official correction to the fake number 555-0177 and confirmed service continuity.
metrics.excellence: PIO proactively activated the alternate 10-digit emergency number (555-0100) via WEA and social media immediately after I-14, preventing misinformation spread; issued a public correction before any media broadcast on the fake number.

metrics.name: Use of Doctrine
metrics.fail: Students failed to cite RCECD-OPS-2026, Section 5, T-2 Contain when initiating firewalling at CAD-FW01 (CYB-DR-1) in I-07; failed to reference EOP 4.3 when activating swatting verification protocol in I-03.
metrics.pass: Students cited RCECD-OPS-2026, Section 5, T-2 Contain when initiating firewalling at CAD-FW01 (CYB-DR-1) in I-07; referenced EOP 4.3 when activating swatting verification protocol in I-03.
metrics.excellence: Students cited RCECD-OPS-2026, Section 5, T-2 Contain before initiating firewalling at CAD-FW01 (CYB-DR-1) in I-07, and referenced EOP 4.3 before activating swatting verification protocol in I-03, demonstrating proactive adherence to doctrine.

hotwash.methodDescription: Use the '3-Up, 3-Down' method by asking each team to share three things that went well and three that broke or failed, going around the room to ensure all voices are heard. Write each response on a whiteboard to create a shared visual record.

questions.text: At the moment you received the SIEM alert (I-02), when did you first stop trusting the CAD system’s integrity, and what specific evidence triggered that loss of trust?

When you saw the ALI data integrity report (I-08), what gap emerged between operations' understanding of the technical situation and the actual state of the network? How did that gap affect your decisions?

At Decision Point I-12, when the structure fire from Marlow was waiting to be dispatched, what would have allowed you to make the switch to manual dispatch using run cards (RCECD-F-11) faster, and what would have let you trust that manual dispatch could maintain service continuity?

When Tamarack County Communications called at I-16b to confirm their call routing and no data corruption, what information or confirmation would have let you decide to activate the backup PSAP (OPS-DR-5) sooner?

After the forensic log (I-10b) confirmed unauthorized admin access via stolen credentials, did you treat that evidence as a technical alert or as a trigger to initiate the cyber incident response protocol? What changed your mind?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: FBI Indianapolis Field Office — Cyber Division (TDoS, Swatting, Extortion)
simcellScripts.trigger: A player contacts the FBI via the 911 Director or the County Information Security Officer
hardQuestions: Do you have the logs preserved? No? Call me back when you have evidence.
Is the ALI data corruption confirmed to be from a malicious actor? If not, you’re not my priority.
What is your timeline for reporting to CISA? We need that within 12 hours.
concessions: Will accept preserved logs and a written timeline.
Will provide a TDoS pattern analysis if you send the ANI list and time windows.
Will defer to CISA for federal coordination if you confirm the cyber incident is active and not a false positive.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: GateKeeper Voice Security (10-digit call-screening appliance vendor)
simcellScripts.trigger: A player contacts GateKeeper to report the silent call flood or to request rule set changes
hardQuestions: You’re trying to activate TDoS-strict rule set? That’s not a standard feature. What’s your ticket number?
The rule set is not enabled by default — you need a signed access request from the Technical Lead.
If you don’t have the ticket number, I can’t assist. We only respond to authorized requests.
concessions: Will enable TDoS-strict rule set if you provide a signed access request (RCECD-OPS-2026, Section 5, T-2 Contain).
Will provide a report on call pattern matching if you send the ANI list and time window.
Will block ANI 555-0105 and 555-0101 if you confirm they’re from spoofed sources.

simcellScripts.trigger: A player contacts Tamarack to confirm rerouting or to report call flow
hardQuestions: We’ve been taking calls on SIP trunk group A since 19:00. What’s your verification plan for the 17 corrupted calls?
How do you know our system is clean? We need a log of your forensic image and backup restore.
If you’re not using our ring-down line, we’re not accepting calls — you’re not in MCTA-2025 yet.
concessions: Will continue to route calls under MCTA-2025 if you confirm your verification plan is complete.
Will provide a call-source analysis if you send the ANI list and time window.
Will accept your forensic image (REC-01) if you provide a signed access request and a hash verification.

simcellScripts.trigger: A player contacts the NOC to report 911 call delivery issues or to request overflow routing
hardQuestions: You’re reporting a TDoS pattern on 911 trunks? What’s your call-source analysis?
We need your ANI list and time window for verification. No report without that.
If you don’t have a signed access request from the Technical Lead, we can’t escalate.
concessions: Will confirm overflow routing to Tamarack County under MCTA-2025 if you provide the ANI list and time window.
Will provide a call-source analysis if you send the forensic logs and ANI list.
Will accept your SIEM alert as a valid incident report if you include the RCECD-OPS-2026, Section 5, T-2 Contain reference.

simcellScripts.trigger: A player contacts RespondCAD to report CAD freeze, unit status issues, or to request a restore
hardQuestions: You’re reporting a CAD freeze? What’s your ticket number?
You need a signed access request from the Technical Lead to restore. No one calls us without that.
If you don’t have a ticket number, we can’t help. We only respond to verified requests.
concessions: Will begin restore from clean backup (2025-12-31 23:59) if you provide a signed access request and a hash verification.
Will provide a forensic report on the session from RCECD-POS09 if you send the SIEM alert and log hash.
Will accept your forensic image (REC-01) if you confirm it was captured before the restore.

warnings.message: Call Taker 4 reports Medic 3 as available but on scene, but the ALI shows 'Unknown' — contradicts C4, which states ALI data is shown where carrier supplies it, so 'Unknown' should not occur for a known unit. (row rewritten once from this note)
warnings.suggestion: Replace 'Unknown' with a valid address from the RCECD ALI database or clarify that ALI data was not received from the carrier.

warnings.message: The 911 call from ANI 555-0105 is reported as silent, but C4 states 911 calls arrive on SIP trunk group A and B, not on 10-digit lines — ANI 555-0105 is a 10-digit line number, not a 911 call. (row rewritten once from this note)
warnings.suggestion: Change ANI 555-0105 to a valid 911 call ANI (e.g., 555-0110) or reassign the call to the 10-digit line 555-0100.

warnings.message: The GateKeeper appliance is not activated, but C1 states the supervisor or Technical Lead must activate the TDoS-strict rule set — the Technical Lead is not authorized to do so alone. (row rewritten once from this note)
warnings.suggestion: Require the Supervisor to activate the rule set, not the Technical Lead, per C1.

warnings.message: The spoofed call from ANI 555-0103 is reported as a red herring, but C4 states 10-digit lines are not routed to CAD — the call should not be considered a system threat. (row rewritten once from this note)
